prompt: A delivery company's on-time rate fell from 96% to 88% in six months. Order volume rose 25% over the same period. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Drivers are likely taking longer routes since a software change.
options.feedback: Nothing mentions new software, and it ignores the 25% jump in volume that lines up with the decline.

options.text: Traffic, weather, routing and staffing each probably contribute something.
options.feedback: This lists causes without committing to one, so it doesn't tell you what to test first.

options.text: Customers are probably giving wrong addresses more often.
options.feedback: Nothing points to addresses, and it ignores the 25% rise in volume over the same six months.

options.text: Capacity has probably lagged the 25% rise in volume.
options.feedback: Right. Volume rose 25% as on-time delivery fell, which points to stretched capacity. I'd compare on-time rates by route against stops per driver.

explanation: The data shows on-time delivery falling from 96% to 88% as volume rose 25%. Likely cause: capacity hasn't kept up. To test it, compare on-time rates with stops per driver by route. If routes with no extra load also slipped, look at routing or the warehouse instead.
